content:
Event 3: First Cloud AI Journey Meetup — Building Cloud & AI Agents for Production Date & Time: Saturday, October 24, 2026 (09:00 AM – 12:00 PM) Location: AWS Vietnam Office, 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower, No. 2 Hai Trieu, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City Role: Intern / Participating Builder (Attendee) Organizers: AWS First Cloud Journey (FCJ/FCAJ) in collaboration with AWS Study Group VN & AWS Student Builder Groups Keynote Speakers & Guest Industry Experts: Mr. Kiet Tran — AI Engineer at Revve AI (AWS Partner specializing in Voice AI Contact Center solutions) Mr. Long Huynh — DevOps Engineer at Styl Solution (Former FCJ Admin) Mr. Thinh Nguyen — DevSecOps & Cloud Engineer at Styl Solution Mr. Xuan An Nguyen — Leader of AWS Student Builder Group at HCMUTE Mr. Khoa Kieu — Technical Lead at Asia Commercial Bank (ACB) Mr. Nghi Danh — AI Engineer at Renova Cloud, AWS Community Builder, Leader of AWS Student Builder Group at HUFLIT Event Check-in & Attendance Event Hall Overview & Attendee Check-in Personal Clear-Face Check-in at the Event 1. Event Atmosphere & Program Background Following the previous two flagship community gatherings — the AWS Community Day in August and the FCJ Build-a-thon Kick-off in September — the First Cloud AI Journey Meetup in October 2026 immersed attendees into a more pragmatic engineering challenge: Bridging the gap between AI Agent prototypes and mission-critical production cloud architectures.
On Saturday morning, the auditorium at the 26th floor of Bitexco was packed with university students from AWS Student Builder Groups alongside experienced software engineers, DevOps specialists, and Tech Leads from leading banks and technology enterprises across Ho Chi Minh City.
The three-hour program unfolded smoothly across 5 intensive sessions: exploring sub-second voice AI conversational pipelines, multi-account network governance, automated AI pentesting, serverless agent core runtimes, and live demonstrations of 24/7 cloud-hosted coding agents.
2. Session 1: Hear, Think, Speak — Building a Low-Latency Voice AI Contact Center on AWS Speaker: Mr. Kiet Tran — AI Engineer at Revve AI (AWS Partner specializing in enterprise conversational AI for commercial banking and enterprise contact centers). Speaker Kiet Tran presenting Voice AI insights Enterprise Revve on AWS Architecture Diagram 2.1. The 200ms Reflex Challenge in Human Conversation Mr. Kiet opened the session with a relatable observation: in natural human conversations, the typical pause between speaking turns hovers around ~200ms. If an automated voice assistant takes longer than 2 seconds of awkward silence to respond, callers will assume the telephone line has dropped.
To address this challenge, he evaluated the trade-offs across three contemporary architectural approaches:
Cascade Architecture (STT ➔ LLM ➔ TTS): The most widespread, battle-tested model running on production today. Incoming audio is converted to text via Automatic Speech Recognition, processed through an LLM for intent reasoning, and transformed back into audio via Text-to-Speech synthesis. Its greatest advantage lies in leveraging state-of-the-art foundation models (such as Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Amazon Bedrock) while allowing fine-grained control over Vietnamese phonetic pronunciation and banking terminology. The primary trade-off is accumulated latency across stages (typically totaling ~1.8 seconds). Speech-to-Speech Architecture (S2S): Native audio-in, audio-out models (such as Amazon Nova Sonic). While offering rapid reflex speeds, Vietnamese conversational inflection remains somewhat unnatural due to current training corpus limitations. Full-Duplex S2S Architecture: An emerging hybrid paradigm pairing a lightweight S2S model at the conversational frontline for immediate reflex responses, backed by a heavyweight LLM operating asynchronously for deep business logic reasoning. 2.2. Engineering Optimizations & Enterprise Banking Architecture To push overall turnaround latency down to ~1.8 seconds, the engineering team at Revve AI implemented two key techniques:
Prompt Caching: Caching the invariant system prompts on Amazon Bedrock, which significantly slashes Time-to-First-Token (TTFT). Natural Conversational Fillers: When the assistant must query an external banking API or database, it dynamically injects subtle conversational filler phrases (“Certainly, please give me just a moment while I pull up those details…”) to sustain conversational continuity without dead air. On the infrastructure side, the solution adheres to rigorous banking compliance:
Call traffic traverses Application Load Balancers into an Amazon EKS cluster hosting SIP servers, WebRTC UDP media servers, and self-hosted STT/TTS models running on GPU instances for accelerated matrix calculations. EKS workers communicate with Amazon Bedrock strictly via AWS PrivateLink, keeping all voice and transcript payloads confined within the private AWS network backbone without routing through public Internet. Customer state and transactional records reside in Amazon RDS Multi-AZ, with call audio archived into Amazon S3 encrypted end-to-end via AWS KMS. 2.3. Live Recruitment Interview Demo on Stage The highlight of the session was a live interactive demonstration. The AI agent, playing the role of “Mai – Talent Acquisition Assistant at May Xanh Cloud Solutions”, dialed direct phone calls on stage to Mr. Kiet and an audience student volunteer to conduct initial candidate screenings for a Cloud Engineer position.
The AI systematically probed candidates with multi-tiered technical questions on 3-tier VPC network topologies, EC2 sizing, S3 lifecycle policies, and RDS high availability. When a student playfully answered that their expected monthly salary was “0 VND”, the AI gracefully adapted with witty humor rather than breaking into repetitive loops.
Mr. Kiet revealed that across an 800-call proof-of-concept, the system achieved a 94% intent routing accuracy, while an automated screening campaign for VPBank reached a 62% completed interaction rate, operating at an economical cost of approximately 3,000 VND ($0.12 USD) per call.
3. Session 2: Multi-Account Resource Management and Sharing with AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) Speaker: Mr. Long Huynh — DevOps Engineer at Styl Solution (Former FCJ Admin). 3.1. Infrastructure Duplication in Multi-Account Environments As companies expand their cloud footprints, infrastructure is naturally partitioned across separate AWS accounts (Dev, Staging, Production, Security, Shared Services). When each account redundantly provisions its own VPC subnets, Transit Gateways, Route 53 Resolver rules, and software licenses, enterprises incur substantial billing waste and operational overhead.
3.2. Core Mechanics of AWS RAM & The Critical AZ ID Gotcha Mr. Long introduced AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) — a complimentary service enabling central owner accounts to securely share infrastructure assets with member accounts across an AWS Organization without duplicating components.
He emphasized an invaluable, hard-earned lesson that often catches cloud engineers off guard:
The Availability Zone Name Trap:
In AWS, logical AZ designations like ap-southeast-1a are randomly assigned per account. The physical facility backing ap-southeast-1a in Account A does not necessarily correspond to the physical facility of ap-southeast-1a in Account B.
When writing Infrastructure as Code (Terraform / CloudFormation) to share subnets across accounts, engineers must explicitly map subnets to physical Availability Zone IDs (AZ ID, such as apse1-az1). Mapping by logical name risks scattering compute across separate data centers, triggering steep and unexpected Cross-AZ Data Transfer charges.
He also clarified the effective permissions evaluation model: an action is only granted when it satisfies the mathematical intersection of all three policy boundaries: RAM Managed Permissions ∩ IAM Policies ∩ Service Control Policies (SCPs) of the AWS Organization.
4. Session 3: Automated Penetration Testing (AI Pentest) with AWS Continuum & AWS Security Agent Speaker: Mr. Thinh Nguyen — DevSecOps & Cloud Engineer at Styl Solution. 4.1. Bottlenecks of Traditional Manual Pentesting Mr. Thinh highlighted three core friction points in conventional penetration testing:
High cost: Commissioning a specialized external security firm typically costs $5,000 to $20,000 USD per assessment. Extended turnaround times of several weeks, making continuous testing incompatible with rapid agile release cycles. Heavy dependency on the individual expertise of the assigned security auditor. 4.2. AWS Security Agent & Dynamic OTP Handling AWS Security Agent (part of the AWS Continuum solution suite) runs on Amazon Bedrock, providing three automated layers across the SDLC:
Design Security Review: Inspects architecture markdown documentation or Terraform definitions pre-deployment to flag design vulnerabilities (200 free reviews/month). Code Security Review: Plugs directly into GitHub/GitLab Pull Requests and CI/CD pipelines to map internal application data flows (1,000 free reviews/month). Automated Penetration Testing: The AI assumes the dual role of user and threat actor, dynamically generating attack graphs to discover and exploit vulnerabilities on live staging websites. A standout engineering tip was his automated workaround for Email OTP authentication: when a web application requires a one-time password delivered via email, Mr. Thinh configured an Amazon EventBridge rule to intercept the inbound email, routed the payload to an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda Function URL enabled to parse the token, and provided that Function URL endpoint directly within the Security Agent’s Login Instructions. The AI agent then programmatically called the endpoint to obtain its own OTP and proceed with authentication.
He stressed a strict rule of thumb: Never run automated AI penetration testing against Production environments; testing must be restricted to SIT or UAT to avoid corrupting live customer state.
5. Session 4: Taking AI Agents from Prototype to Production with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Speaker: Mr. Xuan An Nguyen — Leader of AWS Student Builder Group at HCMUTE. 5.1. Personal Growth & The Prototype-to-Enterprise Divide Mr. Xuan An began with an inspiring personal narrative, recounting his journey from feeling uncertain about career paths as a third-year student to leading the AWS Student Builder Group at Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Education (HCMUTE).
He pointed out that while creating an AI Agent prototype locally with LangChain or CrewAI takes only hours, deploying agents to production serving thousands of concurrent users brings daunting engineering hurdles: isolating multi-tenant conversational state, persisting memory without ballooning token expenses, and maintaining observability under load.
5.2. Exploring Two Core Pillars: Runtime and Memory To address these challenges, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides an integrated serverless platform centered around two foundational pillars:
AgentCore Runtime (MicroVM Sandboxing): Each user session ID is provisioned with an isolated, lightweight MicroVM executing on EC2 Spot instances. This guarantees complete tenant boundary isolation, eliminating cross-session data leakage. Furthermore, compute billing is strictly tied to active I/O computation cycles; during user thinking or idle phases, compute cost drops to zero. AgentCore Memory (Two-Tier Memory Architecture): Short-term Memory: Synchronously retains raw conversational turns for the active session. It supports Memory Branching (resembling Git branches), empowering sub-agents to explore divergent task trajectories without polluting the primary context. Long-term Memory: Asynchronously distills persistent insights across 4 distinct strategies: Conversation Summaries, User Preference profiling, Semantic factual assertions, and Episodic task execution history. 6. Session 5: Kiro & Kiro Crew — 24/7 AI Coding Companion and Automated Code Review Speakers: Mr. Nghi Danh — AI Engineer at Renova Cloud, AWS Community Builder, Leader of AWS Student Builder Group at HUFLIT. Mr. Khoa Kieu — Technical Lead at Asia Commercial Bank (ACB) with over 6 years of engineering leadership. Slide presenting Kiro Crew on the auditorium screen Co-speakers: Nghi Danh and Khoa Kieu 6.1. The Kiro Reel Paradigm: Autonomous Cloud-Hosted AI Mr. Nghi opened the finale session by contrasting the AI tooling landscape on AWS: Amazon Q assists broad workplace tasks, whereas Kiro focuses squarely on software engineering.
The defining breakthrough of Kiro Reel is hosting the AI agent persistently on a cloud server (Amazon EC2 or VPS). Developers are no longer tethered to their laptops; the agent operates continuously 24/7 guided by three principles:
Persistent Memory: Autonomously learns codebase conventions and past code review feedback across sessions without requiring developers to constantly re-upload prompt instructions. Scheduled Cronjobs: Wakes up at off-peak hours (e.g., 3:00 AM) to inspect pending Pull Requests and run maintenance tasks. Human-in-the-loop Guardrails: Routine file editing, linting, and unit test generation execute autonomously; however, any destructive operation (database truncations, environment variable alterations, or infrastructure deployments) triggers an automatic hold requiring human approval. 6.2. 4 Practical Live Demos by Mr. Khoa (ACB Tech Lead) Mr. Khoa mirrored his screen to walk the audience through 4 real-world operational scenarios:
Mobile Ops via Telegram: Linked Kiro Reel to a Telegram bot. While away from his laptop, he sent chat commands from his phone instructing the agent to examine the Talent Radar GitHub repository, author an API endpoint to fetch active customers, and open a ready Pull Request. When asked about RDS database health, the bot queried CloudWatch Logs and reported current CPU utilization and free memory. Automated Infrastructure & News Cronjobs: A 5-minute health check monitored AWS service availability, sending immediate alerts to Telegram upon service degradation; paired with an 8:00 AM daily cron job collecting and summarizing top global AI Agent breakthroughs. Custom “AI Code Reviewer” for Tech Leads: With developer PR volumes surging due to AI tools, a single Tech Lead cannot manually review every pull request. Mr. Khoa uploaded company coding guidelines and security checklists into Kiro Reel’s Knowledge Base. The AI scanned incoming PR diffs, cited exact internal policy clauses breached by specific lines of code, proposed compliant fixes, and posted inline review comments directly onto GitHub. Visual Artifacts Dashboard: Prompted Kiro Reel to scrape IT recruitment portals across Vietnam, generating an interactive salary and tech-stack demand chart directly within the chat window. 6.3. Technical Q&A & Community Minigame Context Window Management: Mr. Nghi detailed Kiro Reel’s Auto-Compact feature (which automatically compresses conversation history at 70% or 90% context saturation) alongside Context Breakdown telemetry, giving engineers full visibility into token consumption across tools, code, and chat history. Interactive Minigame: The room engaged in trivia questions testing concepts of Spec-driven development, Kiro’s 5 client interfaces (IDE, CLI, Reel, Web, Mobile Beta), and multi-provider foundation model support (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek/Kimi). 7. Key Takeaways & Direct Implementation in Project EduMedia AI Attending the First Cloud AI Journey Meetup offered invaluable practical architectural principles that directly shaped and hardened our internship capstone project EduMedia AI (Smart Lecture Storage & Search Engine on AWS):
Key Meetup Principle Architectural Parallel Direct Implementation in Project EduMedia AI Defensive Guardrails & Human-in-the-Loop (Session 5 - Kiro Crew) Protective layers preventing autonomous agents from performing destructive actions or data deletions. Engineered Demo Guardrails into EduMedia AI: flag is_demo_protected blocks deletion requests with an HTTP 403 error, enforces a maximum payload limit of 25MB, and validates MIME types to protect public evaluation sessions. Tiered Memory Decoupling (Session 4 - Bedrock AgentCore) Decoupling short-term in-session conversation records from durable semantic knowledge stores to prevent token bloat. Implemented a two-tier memory design: Amazon DynamoDB persists conversational metadata with automatic S3-offloading when transcripts exceed 250KB; paired with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 (256-d native L2-normalized vectors, 83% smaller than Titan V1 1536-d) for long-term semantic retrieval. Shift-Left IaC Security Review (Session 3 - AWS Security Agent) Validating infrastructure configurations and code within CI/CD pipelines to catch misconfigurations early. Audited the SAM Template under IAM Least-Privilege principles: eliminated all administrative AdministratorAccess or Action: * wildcard permissions and segregated IAM execution roles across all 3 Lambda functions (Ingest, Aggregator, and API). FinOps & Serverless Scale-to-Zero (Session 1 & Session 2) Centralizing resource governance, avoiding cross-AZ billing traps, and optimizing cost models. Built EduMedia AI on a pure Serverless Scale-to-Zero architecture leveraging AWS Lambda and DynamoDB On-Demand. When idle, the system consumes no resources, maintaining fixed baseline expenses at $0.00 USD. Related: 4. Participated Events · 1. Worklog · 5. Workshop · 6. Self-Evaluation

title: S3 Storage & SQS
content:
5.3. Configuring Amazon S3, SQS Buffer Queue, Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) & Event Notifications 1. Amazon S3 Storage Architecture & Security In the EduMedia AI architecture, Amazon S3 acts as the central multimodal Data Lake managing two key object spaces:
uploads/: Raw uploaded media assets (classroom slide captures, lecture voice recordings in .m4a / .mp3). transcripts/raw/: Full-text JSON transcription payloads offloaded from DynamoDB to prevent exceeding the 400KB item size limit. Core Storage Security Baseline: Block All Public Access: Enabled globally to prevent unauthorized data exposure. All client read/write operations must authenticate via time-limited IAM Presigned URLs (15-minute expiration). Server-Side Encryption: Configured by default with AES-256 (SSE-S3) to safeguard data-at-rest. Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS): Permits the React Web Frontend to upload media directly to S3 via HTTP PUT using Presigned URLs: [ { "AllowedHeaders": ["*"], "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "PUT", "POST", "HEAD"], "AllowedOrigins": ["*"], "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"] } ] Figure: Active S3 Buckets provisioned by the SAM CloudFormation stack.
Figure: Verified folder hierarchy (uploads/, thumbs/, and transcripts/) separating raw and derived assets.
Figure: Verified media assets uploaded to the uploads/ prefix via S3 Presigned URLs.
2. SQS Buffer & Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) Architecture Instead of binding S3 events directly to Lambda, EduMedia AI introduces Amazon SQS as a resilient buffer:
SQS Buffer Queue & Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) Architecture 1 • Amazon S3 Upload Event Media files uploaded to prefix uploads/ via Presigned URL trigger s3:ObjectCreated. Prefix: uploads/
Event: s3:ObjectCreated:* 2 • Amazon SQS Buffer Queue Buffers incoming upload events, smoothing traffic spikes and preventing Lambda concurrency exhaustion. Queue: agentsys-ingest-queue
Batch: 5 | Visibility: 720s 3 • AWS Lambda Ingest Worker Consumes messages in batches to trigger Rekognition label/text detection or Transcribe jobs. Function: agentsys-ingest
Timeout: 120s | Memory: 512MB 4 • SQS DLQ & Alarm Poison Pill DLQ & Alarm Isolates malformed media after 3 failed retries, firing immediate CloudWatch alerts to SNS. maxReceiveCount: 3
Alarm: DLQMessagesVisible > 0 Figure: SQS ingestion buffer queue and failure-isolation Dead-Letter Queues.
Architectural Benefits: Traffic Spike Smoothing: If a batch of 50 videos is uploaded concurrently, SQS absorbs the burst and feeds messages progressively to Lambda without exhausting concurrency. Zero Data Loss Isolation: Damaged or corrupted media files are transferred to the DLQ after 3 retries (maxReceiveCount=3), allowing root-cause analysis without breaking pipeline throughput. VisibilityTimeout 720s (6x Lambda Timeout 120s): Aligns with the AWS Well-Architected Framework: SQS visibility timeout must be 6 times the max Lambda execution timeout to prevent redundant duplicate invocations during intensive media workloads. 3. Recursive Event Loop Prevention Crucial FinOps Rule: Subscribing S3 Event Notifications to the entire bucket wildcard s3:* triggers an infinite recursion when Amazon Transcribe outputs a .json transcript → S3 emits an event → Lambda triggers Transcribe → Infinite billing loop!
Enforced Mitigation in EduMedia AI:
Ingestion events are strictly filtered to the prefix Prefix: uploads/. Transcribe outputs are strictly scoped to the prefix Prefix: transcripts/. 4. Testing Media Uploads via Presigned URL # 1. Retrieve API Endpoint and API Key (edumedia-ai or agentsys) API_ENDPOINT=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name edumedia-ai --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='ApiEndpoint'].OutputValue" --output text 2>/dev/null || aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name agentsys --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='ApiEndpoint'].OutputValue" --output text) API_KEY="dev-local-api-key" # Or your configured Parameter ApiKey from SAM deployment # 2. Request a Presigned Upload URL RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_ENDPOINT/api/v1/media/upload-url" \ -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"filename": "test-board.jpg", "content_type": "image/jpeg"}') UPLOAD_URL=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.presigned_url // .upload_url') FILE_ID=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.file_id') echo "File ID: $FILE_ID" echo "Presigned URL: $UPLOAD_URL" # 3. Upload binary image via HTTP PUT curl -X PUT -T "test-board.jpg" -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" "$UPLOAD_URL" Upon successful PUT, S3 automatically forwards the notification to SQS, triggering the background Lambda ingestion.

title: AI Pipeline
content:
5.4. Deploying Lambda Ingestion Engine with Amazon Rekognition & Transcribe vi-VN 1. How the Lambda Ingest Function Operates The agentsys-ingest Lambda function (located in apps/lambda_handlers/ingest.py and apps/workers/ingestion.py) acts as the central multi-modal orchestration engine:
SQS Batch Ingestion: Unwraps s3:ObjectCreated notification batches from SQS. MIME Type Inspection: Automatically detects the media classification: Images (.jpg, .png, .jpeg, .webp): Dispatched to Amazon Rekognition. Audio & Video (.mp3, .m4a, .wav, .mp4): Dispatched to Amazon Transcribe. Metadata & Semantic Aggregation: Aggregates labels, ocr_text, transcript, file dimensions, and timestamps. Invokes Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 to compute a 256-dimensional vector embedding. DynamoDB Persistence: Writes the consolidated record to AgentSysMediaMetadata with status READY. Operational Telemetry: Publishes CloudWatch metrics MediaIngested=1 or MediaIngestFailed=1. Figure: The three AWS Lambda functions (ingest, aggregator, api) orchestrating the media pipeline.
2. Ingestion Processing Flowchart Multimodal Ingestion Pipeline: Vision (Rekognition) & Speech (Transcribe) Step 1 • Ingest Receive & Route Lambda Ingest consumes batch messages from SQS, inspecting MIME type to route to image or audio pipelines. Lambda: agentsys-ingest
Routing: Content-Type check Step 2 • Multimodal AI AI Knowledge Extraction Dispatches to Rekognition (Labels + OCR) or Amazon Transcribe (Vietnamese Speech-to-Text). Rekognition: DetectLabels / DetectText
Transcribe: vi-VN Speech-to-Text Step 3 • Embedding & DB Vector Embedding & Storage Titan V2 embeds unified contextual metadata into 256 dimensions, storing directly to DynamoDB ready for retrieval. Bedrock: Titan Embeddings V2 (256-d)

5.5. Building Multi-modal Search Agent with Amazon Bedrock & DynamoDB GSI Catalog 1. How the Multi-modal AI Search Agent Works In traditional media catalogs, search queries fail when users cannot recall exact keywords. EduMedia AI utilizes Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Nova Pro / Nova Lite) as an intelligent Query Planner coupled with DynamoDB GSI Hybrid Search:
5-Step Pipeline: Semantic Retrieval & Lecture Ranking Step 1 • Client User Query User enters a natural language query in Vietnamese into the search interface. "find derivative formulas and math notes" Step 2 • Bedrock AI Query Planner Amazon Nova analyzes intent, normalizes entities, and generates a structured Search Plan. category: study
subject: math
keywords: derivative, math Step 3 • DynamoDB GSI Candidate Pool Queries partitioned index category-index (avoiding expensive full-table scans). Latency: < 40ms
RCU Saved: 90% Step 4 • Hybrid Scorer Hybrid Scoring Engine Combines semantic vector cosine similarity with exact keyword lexical matching. Titan V2 Vector: 60%
OCR/ASR Lexical: 40% Step 5 • Results Ranked Results Returns ranked lecture materials with precise jump-to timestamps and OCR bounding boxes. HTTP 200 OK
Top-K matches 2. DynamoDB Global Secondary Index Architecture (GSI category-index) Table AgentSysMediaMetadata is configured with GSI category-index:
Partition Key (PK): category (study, videos, receipts, pets, people). Candidate Pool & Ordering: Conforms to Serverless Single-Key design; candidate filtering and descending created_at ordering is performed in Lambda memory on the Candidate Pool (capped at 100 recent items), eliminating complex sort key overhead. Projection: ALL. FinOps & Performance Gains: When the planner identifies category=study, the system performs a targeted Query on partition study instead of a full table Scan → Reduces RCU costs by 90% and cuts latency from 800ms to < 40ms. 3. { "detail": "Cần đăng nhập hoặc X-API-Key hợp lệ" } Unsupported File Format (400 Bad Request) & Over-Limit Upload (413 Request Entity Too Large): Submitting POST /api/v1/media/upload-url with an executable file (malicious.exe, application/x-msdownload) is rejected during MIME/extension validation (endpoints.py): { "detail": "Định dạng tệp không được hỗ trợ. Vui lòng tải ảnh (JPEG, PNG, WebP), âm thanh (MP3, M4A, WAV, FLAC), hoặc video (MP4, MOV, WebM)." } Requesting a presigned URL with size_bytes: 27262976 (26MB > MAX_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_BYTES = 25MB) is blocked before generating an S3 upload URL: { "detail": "Dung lượng tệp (26MB) vượt quá giới hạn demo cho phép (tối đa 25MB)." } Public Demo Sample Protection (403 Forbidden): Calling DELETE /api/v1/media/{file_id} on a record flagged with is_demo_protected: true without the admin override header (x-admin-force: true) returns HTTP 403 to prevent accidental removal of shared sample media: { "detail": "Tệp mẫu được bảo vệ cho người dùng trải nghiệm demo (is_demo_protected: true). Không thể xóa." } Rate Limiting (429 Too Many Requests) & Asynchronous Overload Protection: API Layer (slowapi): The semantic query route /api/v1/media/agent/query (and aliases /api/v1/agent/query, /api/search) enforces 20/minute per client IP (while general routes default to 60/minute in rate_limit.py). Exceeding the quota triggers RateLimitExceeded (HTTP 429): { "error": "Rate limit exceeded: 20 per 1 minute" } Ingest Pipeline Layer (SQS + DLQ): Under ingestion bursts, S3 upload events are buffered in agentsys-ingest-queue and throttled at MaximumConcurrency: 5 on IngestFunction (agentsys-ingest). Messages failing maxReceiveCount: 3 retries are isolated into 3 dedicated Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) monitored by 7 CloudWatch Alarms.

title: Architecture Trade-offs & Enterprise Roadmap
content:
5.7. Discussion: Architecture Trade-offs & Enterprise Roadmap During the initial Proof of Concept (PoC) phase for the First Cloud AI Journey (FCAJ), the core engineering objective for EduMedia AI was to build a production-grade multimodal AI media catalog while adhering strictly to a Zero-Idle-Cost, Lean Serverless architecture.
To strike the right balance between rapid experimental learning and cost-effectiveness, deliberate architectural trade-offs were made. Below is a rigorous technical evaluation of the 5 key limitations of the current architecture along with target enterprise-grade AWS solutions for production scale.
1. In-Memory Vector Search on Lambda RAM Current PoC Status: DynamoDB is a document/key-value NoSQL database without native Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) vector indexing. EduMedia AI implements a Two-Stage Search strategy: Amazon Bedrock acts as Query Planner extracting metadata categories for sub-15ms DynamoDB GSI queries (category-index), followed by in-memory Cosine Similarity scoring over a capped candidate pool (100 newest items) within Lambda RAM. Limitations: While providing zero idle cost, capping the candidate pool at 100 items causes recall degradation when catalogs exceed tens of thousands of items. Conversely, unbounded table scans incur linear O(N) cost and latency penalties. AWS Enterprise Target: Transition to Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (Vector Engine) or Amazon Aurora Serverless (PostgreSQL + pgvector). Vectors are indexed using HNSW or IVF algorithms directly in storage, achieving sub-20ms k-NN retrieval across millions of records without moving raw embeddings into Lambda RAM. 2. Vector Dimensionality & Amazon Titan Embeddings V2 Upgrade Current PoC Status: Earlier implementations subsampled 1536-d vectors to 256-d via uniform index striding to reduce DynamoDB item storage below 400KB limits. Limitations: Neural embedding latent dimensions are non-linear; uniform subsampling degrades topological semantic manifold structure. AWS Enterprise Target: Upgraded to native Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0), which natively supports Matryoshka Representation Learning with direct dimensions: 256 and normalize: true parameterization. Future roadmap includes Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings to unify image, audio, and text vectors into a single joint vector space. 3. DynamoDB Schema & Chunk Scan Overhead Current PoC Status: AgentSysMediaMetadata uses a simple primary key (file_id). Lecture transcript chunks are stored using composite IDs (file_id#CHUNK#0001), requiring DynamoDB FilterExpressions during chunk aggregation. Limitations: FilterExpressions evaluate after disk reads, consuming Read Capacity Units (RCUs) across irrelevant records. AWS Enterprise Target: Normalize to a true DynamoDB Single-Table Design: Partition Key (PK): FILE#<file_id> Sort Key (SK): METADATA or CHUNK#<index> Chunk queries become single partition reads: Query(PK=‘FILE#123’, SK begins_with ‘CHUNK#’) with exact O(k) complexity. 4. Distributed Map-Reduce for Long Lectures Current PoC Status: Upon Transcribe completion, an EventBridge rule triggers a Lambda worker that sequentially refines chunks with Bedrock and performs reduction, paired with DynamoDB Streams for race condition defense. Limitations: For 1-2 hour lectures (40-80 chunks), sequential LLM inference risks hitting Lambda’s execution timeout limit. AWS Enterprise Target: Replace sequential Lambda loops with AWS Step Functions Distributed Map: Split State: Chunk transcript and store in S3/DynamoDB. Distributed Map: Fan-out up to 50 concurrent Lambda workers running Bedrock chunk refinement in parallel. Reduce State: Fan-in and aggregate final structured summaries. Reduces total processing time from minutes to under 10 seconds while eliminating timeout risks. 5. DynamoDB 400KB Item Guard (S3-Offloading) & High-Performance Warm Containers Current PoC Status & Implemented Solution: S3-Offloading (>250KB): DynamoDB enforces a strict 400KB limit per item. Long audio lectures or multi-speaker presentations can produce transcripts exceeding 400KB–1MB. To eliminate ValidationException: Item size has exceeded the maximum allowed size of 400KB, EduMedia AI automatically detects transcripts larger than 250KB, writes the raw full transcript to Amazon S3 (transcripts/raw/{file_id}.json), and stores a 15,000-character preview snippet alongside transcript_s3_uri and has_extended_transcript: true in DynamoDB. The React frontend supports in-modal viewing and direct raw JSON download. Lambda Warm Container Reuse: Preserves Boto3 connection pools and TLS handshakes across invocations, removing cold connection teardowns and saving 50–120ms per SQS message or API request. In-Memory Query Plan Cache (_PLAN_CACHE): Caches parsed search plans in Lambda RAM (LRU, up to 256 entries, 1-hour TTL). Under 50 concurrent requests, this cache provides a 3.74x speedup (reducing mean latency from ~3,194ms down to ~855ms) and saves 100% of LLM token costs on repeated queries. AWS Enterprise Target: Introduce Amazon ElastiCache Serverless (Redis) to share cached query plans across all horizontally scaled Lambda instances. 6. Comparison Summary: PoC vs. Enterprise Production Architecture Technical Criteria EduMedia AI PoC (Current) Enterprise Production Target Vector Search Engine Candidate Pool (100) + In-Memory Cosine Amazon OpenSearch Serverless / pgvector (HNSW) Embedding Space Titan v2 (256-d native) + v1 Fallback Titan Multimodal Embeddings V2 (256-d / 1024-d) Data Model Single PK (file_id) + FilterExpression Composite Key (PK: FILE#id, SK: CHUNK#idx) 400KB Item Size Guard Automated S3-Offloading for Transcripts > 250KB S3 Intelligent-Tiering + OpenSearch Document Pointer Map-Reduce Orchestration EventBridge Worker + Streams Demo AWS Step Functions (Distributed Map State) Container Lifecycle Warm Container Boto3 reuse + LRU _PLAN_CACHE Provisioned Concurrency + ElastiCache Serverless Audio Processing Latency Sequential O(N) per chunk Concurrent O(1) distributed fan-out Idle Infrastructure Cost 0.00 USD / month (Zero-Idle Serverless) ~20 – 50 USD / month (OpenSearch Serverless OCU baseline) Core Objective Cost optimization, rapid lab demo, PoC Scalability to millions of records, Enterprise SLA
